problem: Modular zero-shot ObjectNav systems (e.g. VLFM, ApexNav) focus on producing semantic evidence and scoring frontiers, but re-interpret evidence at every step. The agent can then oscillate between exploration and pursuit, abandon a plausible target near success, or stop from an unverified viewpoint (the 'action consistency gap').
motivation: Detection and semantic scoring have improved, but failures now come from converting evidence into sustained action: commitment, verification and termination. Making commitment persistent and explicit could raise SR/SPL without changing the detector or planner.
key_idea: Add a training-free semantic executive layer (persistent candidate memory, a guarded seven-state finite-state controller, and stability-aware action guards) that turns noisy open-vocabulary evidence into persistent, verifiable, recoverable navigation commitments.
insight: With the perception/mapping/planning stack fixed, gains come purely from executive control. In the HM3Dv2 ablation, the finite-state controller gives the largest step (SR 77.10 to 81.00). Memory gives +0.9 SR and stability control gives +3.2 SR on top. Failure analysis shows timeouts drop (MP3D -10.21%) while frontier exhaustion rises (4.92% to 10.52%), so weak candidates become explicit search failures instead of unstable commitments.
method: Persistent Candidate Memory: nearest-neighbour association within merge radius r_m; EMA position update (lambda=0.3); asymmetric confidence/negative-evidence update; consistency score combining confidence, target ratio, observation count, ITM history and failure penalty; ranked candidate set with stale/failed penalties.

Finite-State Executive Controller: 7 states (Search, Suspect, Approach, Verify, FinalApproach, Failover, Success). Edges are guarded by candidate viability (confidence, consistency, m+>m-), rank persistence and distance (r_v=0.8 m). Verify requires target hits>=2, best distance<=r_stop, confidence, observation count and ITM gate.

Failure loop / Failover: committed states go to Failover, which finishes docking for a verified close candidate, switches to the best unfrozen candidate, or returns to frontier search when no viable candidate or budget remains.

Stability-Aware Action Control: state-conditioned subgoal selection (candidate-conditioned in Approach/FinalApproach, with penalties for visited/failed regions); anti-spin budget; stall detection via progress and best-distance tracker; bounded recovery with negative-evidence updates and B_r-step escape budget.
Verified stop check: STOP only allowed through the semantic-geometric gate (hits, distance, confidence, ITM); unexpected STOPs outside Success are intercepted as recovery or heading reset.
Underlying stack (unchanged): YOLO-World/GroundingDINO detection, MobileSAM, BLIP-2 ITM value maps, frontier planner (ApexNav-style); thresholds fixed across datasets.

setting.backbone: YOLO-World/GroundingDINO + MobileSAM + BLIP-2 (frozen, ApexNav-style stack) with rule-based finite-state executive
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D v1/v2, MP3D); real-world AgileX LIMO robot

numbers.eval_set_note: HM3Dv2: v0.2 validation split, 1000 episodes, 36 scenes
numbers.extra: HM3D-Semantics v0.2; same stack as ApexNav baseline

numbers_note: Table 1 does not name the HM3D splits beyond 'validation'; the split is recorded as 'val'. The failure-cause breakdown is only given in a figure. The real-world result is in a table (40 trials, 100% success) but is not a benchmark.
results: ConsistNav reaches SR/SPL of 84.2/41.2 on HM3Dv2, 63.2/34.8 on HM3Dv1 and 50.6/25.7 on MP3D. It beats the strongest listed baselines (ApexNav 76.2/38.0, 59.6/33.0, 39.2/17.8; SG-Nav 40.2 SR on MP3D). Same-stack gains over the Non-executive baseline are +8.0/+3.2 (HM3Dv2), +3.6/+1.8 (HM3Dv1) and +11.4/+7.9 (MP3D). It reports 40/40 real-world successes on an AgileX LIMO.
limitations: Real-world inference runs on a remote PC (RTX 4090) rather than onboard the robot.
Results depend on coordination between simulator, planner and verified-stop interface. Many thresholds are hand-set and fixed, and the paper leaves adaptive thresholds to future work.
Baseline rows are literature-reported, and the real-world test is small (40 trials, 4 categories, 2 scenes) with no baseline numbers in the table.
